one_month_reasoning: No CIFR earnings fall in the window. No Q3 date has been announced; Q2 was reported Aug 4 and Q3-25 on Nov 3, so Q3-26 most likely lands in the first week of November, just after Oct 31. In-window items: the Oct 28 FOMC (Kalshi hold 72.5c / hike 27.5c, Polymarket hike 24.5c as of Oct 1); late-October hyperscaler capex prints, which drive sector beta; a possible first Barber Lake rent-commencement notice (8-K guides 'Q4 2026', not October specifically, and it is largely priced in); and a possible pipeline lease headline (Odessa is in 'active negotiations'; base rate for a lease signing is a +15-35% day for the signer, but I give it under 10% odds inside one month). The Oct 23 V3 tranche settles a prepaid forward hedged in Nov-2025 (Form 4), so I no longer treat it as new supply. With nothing decisive scheduled I use a symmetric lognormal centred on $15.40 (slightly below spot for volatility drag) with a monthly sigma of 0.31 (112%/3.5). The ladder is effectively unchanged from round 1: removing the V3 'overhang' and a lower fair value roughly cancel over one month, and valuation barely moves a stock over a month. Round 3: the GPU-life rework lowers my 12-month fair value but changes nothing scheduled inside October, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged. Round 4: the discount-rate split and site coverage change nothing inside October, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: 60% split-rate site-level DCF $8.25 (contracted $6.21: AWS in-term at 6.5%, Fluidstack term 7.5%, AI-lab term 7.75%, post-contract and terminal at the 8.0% WACC with an 8.5% exit cap; plus a $1.01B site-by-site pipeline, $2.04) and 40% 14x 2028E EBITDA of $585M plus pipeline, $8.27. Single-rate DCF $7.57. Net debt $5.105B, 495M diluted shares.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-level split-rate DCF at 2027-10-01. Black Pearl (yr-1 $296M, halls Aug-26 to Feb-27, to ~2041-42) and Stingray (yr-1 $107.5M from Apr/May-27 to ~2042), both AWS with Amazon.com guarantee, at 6.5%; Barber Lake Fluidstack term (yr-1 $331.5M, Dec-26/Feb-27 to ~2037, 2.7% refresh-default haircut) at 7.5%; AI-lab years 11-20 (yr-1 $453.6M, 10% haircut) at 7.75%; post-expiry renewals (75% at 85%, 25% vacant 18 months, $2M/IT MW refit) and an 8.5% cap on 2049 cash flow at the 8.0% WACC. EV $8.18B less net debt $5.105B = $3.07B / 495M = $6.21, plus pipeline $1.01B ($2.04) = $8.25. Single 8.0% rate: $7.57. GPU-life sensitivity (split): 5-yr $7.20, 6-yr $8.25, 7-yr $9.18.

inputs_detail.value: Year-1 $296M ($5.5B / sum of 1.03^k, k=0..14), +3%/yr per contract year, 15 yrs per hall: DH1+NH1 50 IT MW Aug-2026, DH2 35 Oct-26, DH3 35 Nov-26, NH2 15 Dec-26, DH4 81 Feb-2027; so expiries run Aug-2041 to Feb-2042. NNN, NOI 98% of rent

inputs_detail.value: Year-1 $107.5M ($2.0B / 18.6), +3%/yr, 20% from Apr-2027 (network hall), 80% from May-2027 (data hall), 15 yrs to ~May-2042; NNN, NOI 98%
inputs_detail.derivation: Inventory figures; the two hall dates are the Stingray deck's rent-commencement dates. The network/data hall MW split is not disclosed, so 20/80 is my judgment.

inputs_detail.input: Barber Lake rent, years 1-10 (Fluidstack, Google backstop)
inputs_detail.value: Year-1 $331.5M ($3.8B / 11.46 at an assumed 3% escalator); Phase I 168 IT MW from Dec-2026, Phase II 39 IT MW from Feb-2027 (8-K: halls Q4-26 to Q1-27); term to ~Dec-2036/Feb-2037; modified gross, NOI 87.5% of rent
inputs_detail.derivation: $3.8B = ~$3.0B (168 MW) + ~$0.83B (39 MW). Escalator rate not disclosed: 3% assumed, as at the AWS leases. 87.5% is the midpoint of the guided 85-90% site NOI margin. Term end moved from Sep-2036 to the hall dates (inventory flag).

inputs_detail.input: Barber Lake rent, years 11-20 (unnamed AI lab, binding commitment)
inputs_detail.value: Year-1 $453.6M ($5.2B / 11.46), +3%/yr, ~Jan-2037 to ~Jan-2047, NOI 87.5%; 10% expected-loss haircut (5-yr life 15%, 7-yr 6%)
inputs_detail.derivation: $5.2B from the 8-K; year-1 is ~5% above the last Fluidstack year, i.e. the 3% escalator carries on. Haircut unchanged from round 3 and inside the supervisor's 10-15% central range.

inputs_detail.value: 15% default probability at the ~2032-33 fleet refresh x 30% of rent unbacked x 60% loss given default = 2.7% of 2033-37 rent (5-yr life 20% default, 7-yr 10%)
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor round-3 correction: the term is not fully Google-backed. The backstop is ~$1.73B vs ~$3.8B of rent (~45%). By 2033 only ~$1.6B of rent remains, so if the backstop is a fixed cap a late default is nearly covered; if it amortises pro rata, 45% is covered. I take ~70% covered, i.e. 30% unbacked. LGD 60% = 18 months' vacancy plus re-letting at 85%. Not double counted with the 7.5% rate: the 7.125% notes that anchor the rate mature in 2030, before the refresh.

inputs_detail.value: 75% renew at 85% of final rent (no downtime), 25% vacant 18 months then re-let at 85%, +3%/yr; refresh capex $2.0M per IT MW on re-let MW, half on renewals (5-yr life 65% / 80% / $2.5M; 7-yr 80% / 90% / $1.5M)
inputs_detail.derivation: Mechanics kept from round 3, which the supervisor judged the soundest structure. Capex is now applied per critical IT MW (216/70/207) rather than gross MW.

inputs_detail.value: 8.5% cap on 2049 cash flow (after both AWS campuses and Barber Lake have reset), discounted at the 8.0% WACC (was 6.75% on 2048)

bear.story: AI-capex digestion deepens (overspend fears, neocloud/AI-lab credit stress). The market values CIFR on contracted assets only, at a 7.5%+ cap / 8.5% discount rate (contracted-only equity $5.5 at a single 8% rate or a 5-yr GPU life, $6.2 at split rates), with no pipeline credit, after Batch Zero verification cuts or delays the Texas GW sites and no new lease is signed. A further Barber Lake overrun beyond the $359M layer or a forced equity raise adds pressure. Bitcoin weakness hurts sentiment. A GPU glut (cheap power plus plentiful Blackwell/Rubin) would cut what tenants can earn on older halls and the market would price weak renewals.

base.story: All three campuses are in rent by mid-2027 and NOI tracks the ~$727M 2028 run-rate. At most one mid-size lease (Odessa/Reveille/Ulysses) is signed, needing parent equity. The stock keeps a pipeline premium over my ~$8.3 fair value, as the sector has throughout 2025-26, but with the 10Y above 5% and fair value below price, it drifts below today's level amid high volatility.

bull.story: One or more large new leases (Odessa conversion, Ulysses, or a Batch Zero GW site with a hyperscaler/AI lab) at strong rents. Base rate: CIFR +19% on the AWS deal (Nov-25), WULF +14% and the sector +11-13% on the Anthropic lease (Jul-26). The AI-infrastructure trade re-rates as it did in Apr-Jun 2026 ($12.9 to $30), and contracted NOI is capitalised near 5.5-6% caps. The 2031 converts move into the money. The GPU-life evidence (old chips kept running, A100 contracts to 2029) supports a power-scarcity premium on powered MW.

thesis_break_reason: Lowered to $7.0, the round-3 supervisor's level. My contracted-only value is $6.21 at split rates ($5.49-6.84 across 5-7-yr GPU lives; $5.53 at a single 8% rate), so at $7.0 the market would pay only ~$0.4B for a 4.6 GW pipeline I value at $1.01B. Getting there would most likely need a fundamental break: a tenant or credit problem in the Fluidstack/AI-lab chain, a large further overrun or delay at Barber Lake/Stingray, a forced dilutive raise, or Batch Zero excluding the Texas pipeline sites.

reasoning: Round 4 makes two fixes. (1) Site coverage: every inventory site now appears once. The three leases are modelled from their own terms (Black Pearl $296M yr-1 +3% per hall to Aug-41/Feb-42; Stingray $107.5M from Apr/May-27; Barber Lake Fluidstack $331.5M from Dec-26/Feb-27 to ~2037, then the AI lab $453.6M to ~2047), replacing the stale deck schedule (2028 NOI $707M vs $727M). Odessa mining is valued to the 2028 halving and its HPC conversion as a 45% branch on the same MW; Colchis at 76%; the Barber Lake and Stingray expansions are added; Canaan shares are credited in net debt. (2) Discounting: AWS in-term rent at 6.5% (the 6.0-6.125% secured notes + 40bp), Fluidstack term at 7.5% (7.125% notes + 40bp), the unrated AI-lab term at 7.75% after a 10% haircut, and everything post-contract, terminal and pipeline at the 8.0% WACC. Supervisor corrections carried: an 8.5% exit cap on 2049 cash flow (was 6.75%) and a small Fluidstack first-refresh default term. I also found my round-3 pipeline NPV/MW mixed a per-gross-MW EV with a per-IT-MW build cost; rebuilt per IT MW with a 10% lower rent, $11.0M build and 8% rate, it is $2.63M/IT MW and the pipeline is $1.01B. Contracted equity: $6.21 split / $5.53 single (round 3 $6.52). DCF: $8.25 split / $7.57 single (round 3 $7.99). EV/EBITDA $8.27. Fair value $8.09 -> $8.26. The 12-month distribution is still dominated by sector beta and lease signings (CIFR 12m log s.d. ~1.0; lease days +15-35%), so the ladders, scenarios and catalysts are unchanged; the thesis break moves to the supervisor's $7.0. Research this round: the inventory and fact-check files, plus one data query (Canaan quote); no web searches. Prior rounds' reasoning on the ladder (mixture of a main lognormal with median ~$14.4 and a 15% bust component at ~$6.0; median ~$12.6, mean ~$16.9) stands.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Tenants' GPU rental price vs launch-era rate: yr1 1.00, yr2 0.80 (next generation ships), yr3 0.55, yr4 0.47, yr5 0.43, yr6 0.38, then a cash tail (yr7 ~0.30, yr8 ~0.15, about break-even after power + colocation). Steep for ~2 years after the successor ships (H100 -50% in 18 months), then flat (A100 23-39% of launch in year 6, V100 ~5% in year 9). For CIFR this drives tenant credit, renewal odds, re-leasing rent and refresh capex at expiry, not in-term rent, which is valued at the contract price.
gpu_life.note: CIFR is a powered-shell landlord; tenants own the GPUs, so in-term rent is valued at the contract price. Life drives (1) renewal odds, re-let rent and refit capex at expiry (5-yr 65%/80%/$2.5M per IT MW; 6-yr 75%/85%/$2.0M; 7-yr 80%/90%/$1.5M), (2) the AI-lab follow-on haircut (15/10/6%) and the new Fluidstack first-refresh default probability (20/15/10%), and (3) the pipeline NPV/IT MW ($2.20/$2.63/$3.02M). Split-rate DCF per share: $7.20 / $8.25 / $9.18. The range narrows slightly vs round 3 ($6.58-9.20) because the 8.5% exit cap gives less weight to the post-expiry years. The 6-yr base is consistent with the fact-checked company lives (CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 since Jan-2026, IREN 5; AMZN cut a subset 6->5). Fact-check corrections applied: the CoreWeave prior-gen pricing quote is 'at or above where it was years ago' (CEO Intrator), and the Kerrisdale margin figures could not be verified (PDF 403), so they are used as direction only.
